subject: Polity
sub_topic: Rajya Sabha — composition and special powers

concepts.name: Rajya Sabha: Constitutional Basis and Nature as a Permanent House
key_dimensions: Article 80 as the constitutional source; Rajya Sabha is NOT subject to dissolution unlike Lok Sabha
Rotational retirement: one-third members retire every two years under Article 83(1)
Contrast with Lok Sabha dissolution under Article 85 — UPSC trap on whether President can dissolve Rajya Sabha (Answer: No)
Implications of permanence: pending bills, committees, and business do not lapse with Rajya Sabha

concepts.name: Composition of Rajya Sabha: Maximum Strength vs. Actual Strength
key_dimensions: Article 80: Maximum strength fixed at 250 — 238 elected representatives of States/UTs + 12 nominated by President
Current actual strength is 245; distinction between constitutional maximum and current operational strength
UPSC trap: 'not more than 250' vs. the common misquote of exactly 250
Fourth Schedule to the Constitution allocates seats to States/UTs — allocation based on population, not equal representation

concepts.name: Nominated Members of Rajya Sabha: Basis, Eligibility, and Rights
key_dimensions: Article 80(3): 12 members nominated by President from fields of literature, science, art, and social service — the four specified fields
Nominated members CAN vote in Presidential election? No — Article 55 excludes nominated members; UPSC classic trap
Nominated members CAN vote in Vice-Presidential election under Article 66 — key distinction from Presidential election
Nominated members can join political parties after nomination and are eligible for ministerial positions

concepts.name: Representation of States and Union Territories in Rajya Sabha
key_dimensions: States are represented based on population (not equal representation) — contrast with US Senate where each state gets equal seats
UTs representation: Only Delhi (NCT) and Puducherry have Rajya Sabha seats among UTs; most UTs have no representation
Article 80(1)(b): Representatives of UTs in Rajya Sabha are chosen in such manner as Parliament may by law prescribe
UPSC trap: J&K reorganization — J&K (now UT) lost Rajya Sabha seats from state quota; Ladakh has no Rajya Sabha seat

concepts.name: Election Method for Rajya Sabha Members: Single Transferable Vote
key_dimensions: Article 80(4): Representatives of each State elected by elected members of State Legislative Assembly by Single Transferable Vote (proportional representation)
UPSC trap: Only ELECTED members of State Legislative Assembly vote — nominated MLAs and MLCs do NOT vote
States with bicameral legislatures: MLCs do NOT participate in Rajya Sabha elections — only MLAs do
Open ballot system introduced to check cross-voting: members must show ballot to party agent — Supreme Court upheld this in Kuldip Nayar case (2006)

concepts.name: Qualification and Disqualification of Rajya Sabha Members
key_dimensions: Article 84: Must be citizen of India, minimum age 30 years (vs. 25 for Lok Sabha), and other qualifications prescribed by Parliament
Domicile requirement removed: The Representation of People (Amendment) Act 2003 removed the requirement to be an ordinary resident of the state one represents
Disqualifications under Article 102: Same as Lok Sabha — holding office of profit, unsound mind, insolvent, not a citizen
Tenth Schedule (Anti-defection): Applies equally to Rajya Sabha members; Speaker equivalent is Chairman of Rajya Sabha

concepts.name: Chairman and Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha: Constitutional Position
key_dimensions: Article 64: Vice-President of India is ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha — NOT elected by Rajya Sabha members
Article 89: Deputy Chairman is elected by Rajya Sabha from among its members — by convention, from opposition party
Chairman cannot vote in the first instance but has a casting vote in case of a tie (Article 100) — same rule applies to Deputy Chairman when presiding

UPSC trap: Removal of Chairman (Vice-President) requires resolution of Rajya Sabha passed by a majority + intimation 14 days in advance (Article 67(b)); Deputy Chairman removed by majority of all then members of Rajya Sabha

concepts.name: Rajya Sabha's Special Power to Create New All-India Services (Article 312)
key_dimensions: Article 312: If Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by 2/3rd majority of members present and voting, Parliament can by law create new All-India Services
This is an EXCLUSIVE power of Rajya Sabha — Lok Sabha has NO role in triggering this power; classic UPSC trap
Existing All-India Services: IAS, IPS, IFoS — created under Article 312; UPSC may test whether a new service has been recently created
Rationale: Rajya Sabha represents states; All-India Services affect state administration; states' consent symbolized through Rajya Sabha resolution

concepts.name: Rajya Sabha's Special Power to Extend Parliament's Legislative Jurisdiction (Article 249)
key_dimensions: Article 249: Rajya Sabha can pass a resolution by 2/3rd majority declaring it necessary in national interest for Parliament to legislate on a State List subject
Effect: Parliament gains power to legislate on that State List item for one year (extendable by further resolutions)
This is EXCLUSIVE to Rajya Sabha — Lok Sabha cannot initiate this process; UPSC trap on which house can do this
Contrast with Article 250 (national emergency), Article 252 (two or more states request), and Article 253 (international treaty) — all other routes for Parliament to legislate on State List

concepts.name: Joint Sitting (Article 108): Rajya Sabha's Exclusion and Limitations
key_dimensions: Article 108: Joint sitting called by President when a bill is rejected by one house, or passed with unacceptable amendments, or not passed within 6 months
Joint sitting is presided over by Speaker of Lok Sabha (NOT Vice-President/Chairman of Rajya Sabha)
UPSC trap — Joint sitting CANNOT be held for: Money Bills (Article 110), Constitutional Amendment Bills (Article 368), and Financial Bills of Category II under certain interpretations
In a joint sitting, Lok Sabha's numerical dominance effectively overrides Rajya Sabha — undermining Rajya Sabha's role as a revising chamber

concepts.name: Money Bills and Rajya Sabha: The Subordinate Role (Articles 109–110)
key_dimensions: Article 109: Money Bills can ONLY be introduced in Lok Sabha; Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations within 14 days
Lok Sabha can ACCEPT or REJECT all or any recommendations of Rajya Sabha on a Money Bill — Rajya Sabha has no veto
If Rajya Sabha does not return the bill within 14 days, it is deemed to have been passed by both Houses

UPSC trap on Article 110 definition: A bill is a Money Bill ONLY if it deals SOLELY with specified matters (taxation, borrowing, Consolidated Fund, etc.) — certification by Speaker is final and not subject to judicial review (though this was questioned in the Aadhaar case 2018)

concepts.name: Financial Bills: Distinction Between Category I and Category II and Rajya Sabha's Role
key_dimensions: Financial Bill (Category I) under Article 117(1): Contains Money Bill provisions but also other matters; can only be introduced in Lok Sabha with President's recommendation but Rajya Sabha has full powers to reject/amend
Financial Bill (Category II) under Article 117(3): Does not contain Money Bill provisions but requires President's recommendation; can be introduced in EITHER house and Rajya Sabha has equal powers
UPSC trap: Category I Financial Bills — Rajya Sabha has more power than on Money Bills (can reject) but less than on ordinary bills (cannot originate)
Joint sitting IS possible for Financial Bills (both categories) unlike Money Bills — important distinction

concepts.name: Constitutional Amendment Bills and Rajya Sabha's Equal Power (Article 368)
key_dimensions: Article 368: Constitutional Amendment Bills must be passed SEPARATELY by each House by special majority (2/3rd of members present and voting + majority of total membership)
There is NO provision for a joint sitting for Constitutional Amendment Bills — Rajya Sabha effectively has a VETO on constitutional amendments
For amendments requiring state ratification (Article 368(2) proviso): Ratification by not less than half the state legislatures required additionally
UPSC trap: This gives Rajya Sabha enormous power — even a government with brute majority in Lok Sabha cannot amend the Constitution if Rajya Sabha blocks it

concepts.name: Rajya Sabha's Role in National Emergency, President's Rule, and Other Emergencies
key_dimensions: Article 352 (National Emergency): Proclamation must be approved by BOTH Houses within one month by special majority; Rajya Sabha cannot be bypassed
Article 356 (President's Rule): Approval needed from both Houses; if Lok Sabha is dissolved, Rajya Sabha alone can approve it (critical role due to Rajya Sabha's permanent nature)
Article 360 (Financial Emergency): Same — requires approval of both Houses; Rajya Sabha's permanence ensures continuity

UPSC trap: During National Emergency, Lok Sabha's term can be extended but Rajya Sabha continues — this means Rajya Sabha alone can revoke emergency if Lok Sabha is not in session? No — revocation requires Lok Sabha special sitting

concepts.name: Removal of High Constitutional Functionaries: Rajya Sabha's Initiating Role
key_dimensions: Impeachment of President (Article 61): Can be initiated in EITHER House of Parliament — Rajya Sabha can initiate
Removal of Vice-President (Article 67): Resolution for removal must be initiated in Rajya Sabha ONLY — Lok Sabha only concurs; this is EXCLUSIVE to Rajya Sabha
Removal of Supreme Court/High Court judges (Article 124/218): Address can be initiated in EITHER House
UPSC trap: Vice-President's removal is the ONLY constitutional removal process that must ORIGINATE exclusively in Rajya Sabha — not even impeachment of President has this restriction

concepts.name: Term of Rajya Sabha Members and Mid-term Vacancies
key_dimensions: Article 83(1): Rajya Sabha members serve a term of 6 years; retirement in rotation — one-third retire every two years
Mid-term vacancy: A member elected to fill a casual vacancy serves only the REMAINDER of the original term, NOT a fresh 6-year term

UPSC trap: A member elected for a short remainder term (even less than 1 year) is still counted as one full 'term' for purposes of disqualification provisions? No — only full terms count for the concept of 'consecutive terms' in certain contexts
Rajya Sabha election schedule is governed by the Representation of the People Act, 1951 — elections held before the due date of retirement

concepts.name: Privileges of Rajya Sabha and Its Members (Articles 105 and 194)
key_dimensions: Article 105: Freedom of speech in Parliament; no member liable to court proceedings for anything said or any vote given in Parliament
Powers, privileges, and immunities of Rajya Sabha are the SAME as Lok Sabha — there is no differentiation in Article 105
Rajya Sabha can punish for breach of privilege and contempt — Chairman has powers similar to Speaker in this regard
UPSC trap: Privilege motion in Rajya Sabha — can be raised against a Minister who is a member of Lok Sabha? Yes, if the statement was made in Rajya Sabha or relates to Rajya Sabha business

concepts.name: Rajya Sabha and the Federal Character: Comparison with Upper Houses Globally
key_dimensions: Rajya Sabha is NOT a truly federal chamber — states do not have equal representation (unlike US Senate); seats allocated by population
Rajya Sabha members elected by State Legislative Assemblies (not directly by people) — indirect election weakens its democratic legitimacy but strengthens its role as a states' representative body
Rajya Sabha lacks the power to block Money Bills — unlike the German Bundesrat which has strong veto on federal legislation affecting states

UPSC analytical angle: Despite being called 'Council of States,' Rajya Sabha's special powers (Articles 249, 312) are more about national interest than state protection — a constitutional paradox frequently examined

concepts.name: Sessions of Rajya Sabha and Quorum Requirements
key_dimensions: Article 85: President summons, prorogues Parliament; Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved but can be prorogued
Article 100(3): Quorum for Rajya Sabha is 1/10th of total membership = 25 members (if total strength is 245)
UPSC trap: If quorum is not present, Chairman must either adjourn or suspend until quorum is present — business transacted without quorum is NOT automatically void
Rajya Sabha sittings: No constitutional minimum number of days prescribed; by convention, Parliament should sit for a minimum number of days (recent controversy over fewer sitting days)

concepts.name: Rajya Sabha's Role in Approving Delegated Legislation and Subordinate Legislation
key_dimensions: Certain rules/regulations framed under statutes require 'laying before both Houses of Parliament' — Rajya Sabha has equal role in scrutinizing delegated legislation
Committee on Subordinate Legislation exists in both Houses separately — Rajya Sabha has its own such committee
UPSC trap: When a statute says 'subject to modification by Parliament' — this means BOTH Houses must approve the modification; Rajya Sabha cannot be bypassed
Recent controversy: Rules under Article 370 abrogation process — whether Rajya Sabha's role in approving Presidential Orders was adequate; raises questions about parliamentary oversight
